login.title: Sign in to rpmgr
login.codeHint: Enter the code your authenticator app shows, or one of your recovery codes.
login.wrongPassword: The e-mail address or the password is wrong.
login.wrongCode: The code is wrong or was used already. Try the next code.
login.tooMany_one: Too many attempts. Try again in {{count}} second.
login.tooMany_other: Too many attempts. Try again in {{count}} seconds.

link.incomplete: This link is incomplete. Open the whole link you were given, or ask for a new one.

setup.title: Create the first account
setup.intro: This account becomes the Owner of the first organisation and the Instance Admin.
setup.name: Your name
setup.exists: The first account exists already. Sign in with it, or ask for a reset link.

reset.title: Set a new password
reset.passwordHint: 12 to 256 characters. A passphrase of several words is easy to type and hard to guess.
reset.done: Your password is set, and your other sessions have ended. Sign in with the new password.

forgot.title: Reset your password
forgot.sent: If an account uses this address, a reset link is on its way. It works once, for 24 hours.
forgot.noMail: This controller cannot send e-mail. Ask an Owner or the Instance Admin for a reset link.

stepUp.title: Confirm it is you
stepUp.intro: This action needs you to confirm your identity again. You stay confirmed for a few minutes.
stepUp.wrongCode: The code is wrong or was used already. Try the next code.

account.title: Account
account.passwordChanged: Your password is changed, and your other sessions have ended.

mfa.title: Two-factor authentication
mfa.none: Add an authenticator app, so that signing in needs a code from your phone as well as your password.
mfa.scan: Scan this code with your authenticator app, then enter the 6-digit code it shows.
mfa.qr: QR code for your authenticator app
mfa.manual: Or enter this key by hand:
mfa.codesIntro: Keep these recovery codes somewhere safe. Each works once instead of a code from the app, and they are shown only now. Your other sessions have ended.
mfa.removeWarning: Removing the authenticator lets your password alone sign you in, and ends your other sessions.
mfa.required: An organisation you belong to requires two-factor authentication. Set up an authenticator to continue.

tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.intro: Personal tokens for the command line and scripts. A token can do only what its scopes allow, and never more than your role.
tokens.name: Name
tokens.created: Copy the token now. It is shown only once.

scope.routes_write: routes, targets, health checks and access policies
scope.infrastructure_write: gateways, gateway groups, port pools, domains and certificates
scope.audit_read: read and export the audit log
scope.org_write: SSO, the MFA policy and the org's settings
scope.instance_admin: the instance: CA, KEK, system gateways and instance settings

route.title: Route {{name}} ({{type}})
route.notFound: This route does not exist, or you cannot see it.
route.mtu: UDP datagrams travel as QUIC datagrams up to about 1240 bytes, or 1412 bytes once path-MTU discovery has run. Larger ones go over the flow's stream: delivered reliably, but one late packet holds up those after it.
route.fallback: served over TLS and HTTP/2, the fallback for QUIC
route.changed: The route changed since this page loaded it. The page shows it as it is now; try again.

notServing.BLOCKED_BY_LOCAL_POLICY: blocked by the connector's local policy
notServing.POLICY_INVALID: the connector's local policy does not load
notServing.PORT_IN_USE: the port is in use on the gateway
notServing.TRANSPORT_UNAVAILABLE: no data session over the route's transport
notServing.NO_DATA_SESSION: no data session to the connector

apply.pending: Revision {{seq}}: applied by {{applied}} of {{total}} agents so far.
apply.timeout: Revision {{seq}}: an agent did not answer in time.
apply.offline: Offline, they get it when they connect: {{agents}}

fields.name: Name
fields.maxBody: Largest request body (bytes, 0 for no limit)

hints.pairs: One per line, as key=value or Name: value.

transport.default: The connector's or the instance's default
transport.auto: QUIC, falling back to TLS and HTTP/2

conflict.title: The route changed since you opened it
conflict.changedBy: Changed by {{by}} {{when}}. Your changes are not saved yet.
conflict.changed: Changed {{when}}. Your changes are not saved yet.
conflict.onTop: Put my changes on the new version

routeNew.title: New route
routeNew.groupNeeded: Choose the gateway group that serves the route.

preview.title: Preview
preview.connectors: Connectors its streams would go to: {{names}}

targetForm.connectorNeeded: Choose the connector that reaches the target.
targetForm.caBundle: CA bundle ID (empty: the system's roots)
targetForm.spki: Public key pin, SHA-256 in hex (optional)

connectors.title: Connectors
connectors.notFound: This connector does not exist, or you cannot see it.
connectors.controlUp: Control session up from {{addr}}, last seen {{when}}.

transportSetting.AUTO: QUIC, falling back to TLS and HTTP/2

connectors.noRoutes: No route has a target on this connector.
connectors.changed: The connector changed since this page loaded it. The page shows it as it is now; try again.
connectors.decommissionWarning: Decommissioning {{name}} revokes its identity and ends its sessions for good; it cannot enroll again with it. Its route targets stay, serving nothing, until they are removed.

enroll.title: Enroll a connector
enroll.ephemeral: Ephemeral: removed 30 minutes after it last disconnects
enroll.uses: Enter a whole number, 0 for any number.
enroll.targetsHint: One per line, as ip:port, [ipv6]:port or a socket path. The installer writes them into the host's local policy; without any, the connector reaches nothing until one is allowed.
enroll.step2: 2. When the installer asks for it, paste this token. It is shown only now.
enroll.note: The token is never part of the command line, and it expires in {{lifetime}}.
enroll.waiting: Waiting for the connector to enroll and connect…
enroll.noTokens: No enrollment token can enroll a connector now.

gateways.title: Gateway groups
gateways.noGroups: The org has no gateway group yet.
gateways.notFound: This gateway group does not exist, or you cannot see it.
gateways.hostnamesHint: One per line: the names public traffic reaches the group's gateways by.
gateways.cidrsHint: One CIDR per line: proxies in front of the gateways whose X-Forwarded-For the gateways keep.
gateways.noGateways: The group has no gateway yet.

gwActions.endpointsHint: One host:port per line: where connectors reach this gateway, its own address, not the group's.
gwActions.drainHint: Stops new public connections, and ends the open ones after the gateway's drain period.
gwActions.tokenIntro: A token that enrolls {{name}} and nothing else, valid for 1 hour. Making it needs you to confirm it is you.
gwActions.decommissionWarning: Decommissioning {{name}} revokes its identity and ends its sessions for good; its tunnel endpoints stop serving.

pools.title: Port pools
pools.none: The group has no port pool: TCP and UDP routes have no public ports.
pools.range: Ports are 1 to 65535, the first no larger than the last.
pools.quotasIntro: How many ports of the group's pools the org's routes may hold. Empty: the pools alone limit them.

domains.title: Domains
domains.none: The org has no domain claim. Routes need a verified domain for their hostnames.
domains.method: How to prove it is yours

methods.http: An HTTP token, served by your gateways

domains.txtHow: Create this TXT record at your DNS provider, then check now:
domains.httpHow: Point the name at one of the org's gateways; they serve the token at {{url}}. Then check now. The token is:

pem.file: Or read it from a file:
pem.fileSecret: Or read it from a file; it stays in this page until you send it:

certs.title: Certificates
certs.none: The org has no certificate yet. HTTP routes with ACME get theirs on their own.
certs.renewQueued: A renewal is under way already.

bundles.title: CA bundles
bundles.none: The org has no CA bundle. HTTPS targets are verified with the system's roots unless they name one.

policies.title: Access policies
policies.none: The org has no access policy.
policies.rules: Rules, in the order they apply

routePolicies.title: Access policies
routePolicies.none: The route applies no access policy: every client reaches it.
